newsitem.title: CHILE: Escondida workers to vote Wednesday on strike.
newsitem.headline: Escondida workers to vote Wednesday on strike.

text.p: Striking workers at Chile's Escondida copper mine will vote Wednesday on whether to continue the five-day-old walkout or accept the company's latest wage offer, union president Hugo Fernandez said.

The roughly 350 workers on strike, out of a total workforce of 2,000, will vote as of 1000 local/1400 GMT in Antofagasta on whether to accept the wage offer, Fernandez told Reuters. No result from the vote was expected until about 1900/2300 on Wednesday, he said.
He declined to say whether he thought workers might accept the pay offer, identical to one offered by Escondida before the strike began Friday, he said.
"The union leadership has done what it can. Now it's up to the workers," he said by telephone from Antofagasta.
But the mere fact that a vote has been called at all, without a new pay offer, suggests support for the strike may be petering out.
Fernandez said the strike had stopped about 60 percent of activity at the open pit mine. Escondida's CEO Ken Pickering said Monday activity at the mine was cut only by about 15 percent.
Owned by Broken Hill Proprietary and RTZ Corp plc, the mine produces about 800,000 tonnes of copper a year, most of it contained in concentrates though it also has a cathodes plant.
